contract: C11, docs/protocol.md. The relay (stage 3) checks its model against these vectors; the daemon (stage 4) gives the socket path and end_scope. Every value is a sample; the list of the samples' scope is ["a.example"]. Since board ab-v16.30 the vectors hold the per-scope rules (the no-list 503 and the 1008 closes, the refusals per scope), and since board ab-v16.50 the peer check in place of the key (the peer's and the session's 403, the order of the checks, the session check with a fake process table, the defensive root rules and the 1008 close of a root that left): the relay meets them from part 2 (boards ab-v16.35 and ab-v16.51) on.
scopeListNote: The list of the samples' scope: the refusals and passes per scope are checked against it.
mainFrameIdNote: The id of the sample tab's own target: a Page.navigate with this frameId, or with none, navigates the main frame.

upgradeChecksNote: The order of the checks before the upgrade (C11). peerCheck: the relay runs with --peer-check. relay: the link, bridge.info (1 or more: an answer; 0: too old; null: no answer yet), the name of the last allowlist line (lines) or null, and with the peer check the result of its self-test (selfTest: the form pidfd, stat or mac, or failed). peer (with the peer check): what the relay reads at the accept: read (SO_PEERCRED or LOCAL_PEERPID answered), pid, uid (own: the relay's), in the pidfd form pidfd (null: SO_PEERPIDFD failed; poll: what libc poll returns, 0 not readable, 1 readable, -1 an error; fdinfoPid: the Pid: line of its fdinfo), in the stat form and on the Mac start (the start time at the accept; null: not readable). world: the table of procs that the walk and the cgroup reads see; procs (optional): entries of that table that this case replaces (gone: true removes the pid). answer: the id of an upgradeAnswers entry (the session's 403 with the peer's pid in <pid>), or status 101 (the upgrade).
